en: Now if we take a look at the issue refund
tool down here,
it's interesting to see that in there
we have logic for
loading
an order from a JSON file that is our
database here. In the end, that is simply
that orders.json file which we have. And
actually that orders.json file is outside of
the sandbox. I accidentally moved it there
before, but it's outside of the sandbox.
And that is also hardcoded here because that
acts as our database, simulates a database
here. We load the order from there,
and that allows the agent to try to issue a
refund for a given order
wanting the order ID.
And actually, I'll mirror it into the
sandbox as well. This orders.json file could
be edited. This one out here can't be
because it's outside of the sandbox. I'm
just also putting it in the sandbox and look
up orders so that we could ask for a refund
for a specific customer, for example, and
the agent could then find the order ID.
That's why I'm mirroring it in there. And
what we're then doing in issue refunds is
we're taking a look at what the refund
amount would be. And then we're checking if
the amount of
cents in the end, so the amount of money we
want to refund is above a certain threshold,
which is configurable, which in my case is
1,000 cents, so $10.
And if it is above that threshold, we
actually don't auto approve. Instead, we
trigger another function, request refund
approval. And that is a function where I
simply ask the user who's using the agent
for approval.
So I'm taking a look at the user's answer
expecting Y or
N. N is the default. If the user basically
does not enter a Y, it's not granted, or Y
or yes to be specific.
So I then take a look at the answer and
simply return whether it is Y or yes. And if
it's not, it's denied, it's not granted.
And then down here I get approved back. That
is basically true or false. So was it Y or
yes, then it's true, otherwise it's denied.
And if it's not approved, we return a tool
call result to the model which requested the
tool call, of course, as you learned, that
the refund was not granted, that the human
approval was denied.
And otherwise, if we make it past this
check, if the human did approve, we actually
execute that refund. We simulate it here in
this code.
And then we'd return a different response to
the model telling it that the refund was
performed.
